name: Tibni
title: Rival King over Israel
summary: Tibni, son of Ginath, was a rival to Omri for the throne of the Northern Kingdom of Israel after the death of King Elah. The people of Israel were divided into two factions—one half followed Tibni, and the other followed Omri. In the end, Omri's supporters prevailed, and Tibni died, so that Omri became sole king over Israel.

keyEvents.title: Zimri's Coup and Death
keyEvents.description: After Zimri killed King Elah and seized power, but was besieged by the army under Omri, Zimri burned himself alive. This created a power vacuum in Israel.

keyEvents.title: The People Divided Between Tibni and Omri
keyEvents.description: After Zimri's death, the people of Israel were split into two camps: half followed Tibni, son of Ginath, and wanted to make him king, while the other half followed Omri.

keyEvents.title: Omri's Supporters Defeat Those of Tibni
keyEvents.description: Those who followed Omri overcame those who followed Tibni, son of Ginath. Omri's faction proved stronger in the struggle for power over the throne of the Northern Kingdom.

keyEvents.title: Death of Tibni
keyEvents.description: Tibni died, and thus Omri became the sole king over Israel. The Bible gives no further details about the circumstances surrounding Tibni's death, but it is implied that it occurred as a result of civil war.

keyEvents.title: Omri Becomes Sole King
keyEvents.description: After Tibni's passing, Omri began to reign as the undisputed king over all Israel, and he later founded the city of Samaria as the new capital.
